name: sox
one_line: the Swiss Army knife of sound processing
plain: `sox` converts, trims, speeds up, reverses and analyses audio files. Its companion `play` plays a file and `rec` records. For CTF audio puzzles it is quick for the jobs that need no window: reverse a clip, change its speed, draw a spectrogram, read the statistics.
The shape is `sox [global options] INPUT [format options] OUTPUT [effect ...]`. Effects come last and are chained left to right.
when: Draw a spectrogram of a suspicious sound.
Reverse, speed up or slow down a clip.
Convert between WAV, MP3, FLAC and raw data.
Trim a short piece to listen to it.

examples.title: File information
examples.explain: soxi prints sample rate, channels, length and encoding. A strange sample rate (such as 8000 or 44100) sometimes matters.

examples.title: Spectrogram picture
examples.explain: -n is the null output (nothing but the effect). Open spec.png: images or text drawn in the spectrum appear.

examples.title: Change speed
examples.cmd:
sox sound.wav slow.wav speed 0.5
sox sound.wav fast.wav tempo 2
examples.explain: `speed` changes pitch and speed together, `tempo` changes speed only.

examples.title: Trim a piece
examples.explain: Start at 10 seconds and keep 5 seconds.

examples.title: Statistics
examples.explain: Prints duration, amplitude and the DC offset: a quick sanity check.

examples.title: Convert to raw bytes
examples.explain: Turns the audio into bytes you can inspect with xxd or a script.

examples.title: Treat a raw file as audio
examples.explain: Give the file's shape (rate, encoding, bits, channels) so sox can play bytes that are not a real audio file.

examples.title: Play a file
examples.explain: Listen to the clip from the command line.

options.plain: Null file: no input or no output.

options.flag: effect: speed F / tempo F / pitch CENTS
options.plain: Change speed, tempo only, or pitch only.
Draw a spectrogram PNG (-x width, -y height, -z dynamic range).
Pick or mix channels, change the sample rate.

mistakes: Reading raw bytes with the wrong rate/bits/encoding and hearing noise: try the common shapes (8000 Hz, unsigned 8-bit, mono).
Forgetting -n when you only want an analysis effect.
Using speed when you wanted tempo (the pitch changes).
try: Make a spectrogram of a WAV and read it.
Reverse a recording of your own voice.
Slow a Morse clip with tempo and decode it.
Turn a small binary file into audio with the raw options.
see_also: ffmpeg(1), soxi(1), play(1), Audacity, Sonic Visualiser, minimodem(1), multimon-ng(1).
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
